Device.description: Device is what an inspection found of one device.

advice.description: Advice says what the operator can do, in a sentence or two.

coverages.description: Coverages and Observations count its other stored rows: the sets of facts its gathers covered, and its gathers.

device.description: Device is the device's inventory name.

id.description: ID is the device's ID, which the controller's log names.

keyed_by.description: KeyedBy is each key identity its rows name, with how many name it, at most eight.

keyed_by_more.description: KeyedByMore counts the rows under key identities past the eight named, which only an edited database holds.

observations.description: Coverages and Observations count its other stored rows: the sets of facts its gathers covered, and its gathers.

repairs.description: Repairs names the repairs that apply: discard, truncate. Empty when there is nothing to repair. Truncate is named only when it would keep some of the history. With Unverifiable, each takes its flag.

sealed_under.description: SealedUnder is each master key version its sealed rows' payloads name, with how many name it and whether the inspection was given a key for it, at most eight. A row under a version it was not given cannot open.

sealed_under_more.description: SealedUnderMore counts the sealed rows under versions past the eight named, which only an edited database holds.

state.description: State is how its stored history stands. Known values: empty, healthy, rekey_pending, refused, broken, mixed_keys, other_keys, unopened, partly_unopened. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

truncate_from.description: TruncateFrom is the gather a truncate would cut the history at: the one that wrote the last stable row that verifies before the first that fails. That gather and every later one are removed whole, since a row missing after the last that verifies could be any of theirs; a failing volatile row is removed alone, and its gather kept. Absent when no stable row fails, or no truncate applies.

under.description: Under is the history checked under each key the inspection was given, current first.

unverifiable.description: Unverifiable is true when nothing the inspection was given can tell whether the history is damaged: some row does not open (unopened, partly_unopened, or such a row in any other state), or its rows name another facts key or both (other_keys, mixed_keys). Each repair of such a history takes the flag that names it: discard's --discard-unverifiable-history, truncate's --truncate-unverifiable-history.

KeyCheck.description: KeyCheck is a device's history checked under one set of keys.

checked.description: Checked is how many rows, in the order they were stored, passed before the first that failed: all of them when none did.

failed.description: Opened and Failed count the rows that open as the device's own under these keys and the ones that do not, each row checked on its own.

failure.description: Failure is the first row that fails, absent when none does.

key_id.description: KeyID is the identity of the keys.

opened.description: Opened and Failed count the rows that open as the device's own under these keys and the ones that do not, each row checked on its own.

role.description: Role is current or previous. Known values: current, previous. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

verifies.description: Verifies is true when every row opens as the device's own under these keys and the chain over its stable rows is whole.

KeyedRows.description: KeyedRows is one key identity a device's rows name.

key_id.description: KeyID is the identity, as the rows name it: never the key.

role.description: Role is current, previous or other. Known values: current, previous, other. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

rows.description: Rows is how many rows name it.

Keys.description: Keys names the facts keys an inspection or a repair read with.

current.description: Current is the identity of PLEIADES_FACTS_DIGEST_KEY's keys, absent when it was not set.

previous.description: Previous is the identity of PLEIADES_FACTS_DIGEST_KEY_PREVIOUS's keys, absent when it was not set.

RowFailure.description: RowFailure is one stored row that fails a check.

chain_index.description: ChainIndex is its place among the device's stable rows, from 0, as the fact chain route numbers a break; absent for a volatile row.

fact.description: Fact is the fact the row holds, given only with --show-fact-names and only when its payload opens.

key_id.description: KeyID is the key identity the row names.

kind.description: Kind is why it fails. Known values: unsealed, does_not_open, token_mismatch, hash_mismatch, chain_missing, chain_link_mismatch, chain_hash_mismatch. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

observation.description: Observation is the number of the device's gather that wrote it.

observed_at.description: ObservedAt is when the value it holds was first observed.

position.description: Position is its place among the device's rows, from 0, in the order they were stored.

row.description: Row is the row's ID in the facts table.

sealed_version.description: SealedVersion is the master key version the row's payload names, absent when it is not sealed.

stable.description: Stable is true for a stable row, false for a volatile one.

Rows.description: Rows counts a device's stored facts.

stable.description: Total is every row; Stable and Volatile split it by kind.

total.description: Total is every row; Stable and Volatile split it by kind.

unopened.description: Unopened counts the rows whose sealed payload does not open under the master keys the inspection was given, whatever facts key they name.

volatile.description: Total is every row; Stable and Volatile split it by kind.

SealedRows.description: SealedRows is one master key version a device's sealed rows name.

role.description: Role is current when it is the inspection's MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION, previous when it is its MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS_VERSION, and other when the inspection was given no key for it, so that none of these rows opens. Known values: current, previous, other. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

rows.description: Rows is how many rows name it.

version.description: Version is the version tag the rows' envelopes carry, as MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION named it when they were sealed: an identifier stored in the clear, never part of a key.

description: Report is what one inspection found: the keys it read with, and each device it reports. Printed by controller facts inspect --json. schema_version is the major version: it goes up only for a change an existing reader could misread, a field removed or renamed or given another type or meaning. Within a major version a newer producer may add fields, and new values to the open sets (a state, a failure kind, a role, a repair). So a reader ignores a field it does not know, treats a state it does not know as needing repair, and refuses a major version it does not know.

advice.description: Advice is said of the fleet as a whole when what it found points at the command's own settings rather than at any device: every device read under another facts key, every one with no row that opens, or any one holding rows that do not open (naming the master key versions they are sealed under that the command was not given). Absent otherwise.

devices.description: Devices are the devices reported: the one asked for, or in a fleet inspection every device whose state is not empty or healthy (all of them with --all), in the order of their database IDs.

keys.description: Keys are the identities of the facts keys the inspection read with, never the keys themselves.

needs_repair.description: NeedsRepair is how many of them hold a history no controller with these keys can serve (State.NeedsRepair).

scanned.description: Scanned is how many devices were read.

schema_version.description: SchemaVersion is this document's major version.

scope.description: Scope is device when one device was asked for, fleet when every device holding stored facts was read. Known values: device, fleet. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

title: Pleiades facts inspection
